note: Task #106: profile-generation performance, measured, not assumed. Two distinct costs are reported separately because they are NOT the same thing -- collapsing them would misleadingly call the whole pipeline 'cheap'.

reanalysis_only_cost.description: scripts/build_model_profile.py: pure reanalysis of Phase 11C's ALREADY-EXISTING raw ablation JSONL (rankings.json), zero new inference. This is the only step that is genuinely cheap.
reanalysis_only_cost.method: 5 repeated runs, timed via the standard time(1) utility (wall clock + max RSS), both models built per run
reanalysis_only_cost.conclusion: genuinely cheap: well under 1 second, well under 20MB RSS, for both models combined

raw_ablation_sweep_cost.description: The cost this reanalysis is NOT counting: producing the raw per-layer single-ablation data in the first place (what Phase 11C actually ran, and what a brand-new model would require before any profile could be built at all -- this is the real, non-cheap cost of a model-specific profile).
raw_ablation_sweep_cost.phase11c_original_sweep_not_separately_t: Phase 11C's original 135M/360M raw ablation sweeps (32 configs x 31 prompts each) were not instrumented with per-run wall-clock logging at the time, so their exact historical duration cannot be reported here.
raw_ablation_sweep_cost.current_measurement_basis: Task #98's live 360M held-out naive-layout sweep (this same phase, same host, same build-cpu-rc1 binary, CPU-only, ctx=2048, gen_tokens=32), which is directly comparable in per-run shape (one membrane-kv-mixed-layer invocation per config, 10 prompts per invocation)
raw_ablation_sweep_cost.measured_360m_rate: 5 completed runs in 235 elapsed seconds = ~47s per 10-prompt run

extrapolation_to_a_full_31_prompt_32_con.method: 47s/run * (31 prompts / 10 prompts) * 32 configs, linear in prompt count -- an ESTIMATE, not a direct measurement

raw_ablation_sweep_cost.caveat: This is an order-of-magnitude estimate extrapolated from a same-session, same-host, comparable-shape measurement -- not a re-run of the actual full ablation sweep. It should be read as 'on the order of an hour on this CPU-only host for one model', not as a precise figure.

conclusion: The reanalysis step alone (what most of Task #95/#96 actually ran) is genuinely sub-second and cheap. The step that makes a NEW model's profile possible in the first place -- the raw per-layer ablation sweep -- is on the order of an hour of CPU-only inference per model on this host, and must not be described as cheap or ignored when scoping how expensive it is to onboard a new model to this workflow.
